sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r13/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 13 (check 12) and Internal Quality Checks row 13 (no extra annotation or cell comment on this row)
evidence: task/task.toml [environment] holds exactly four keys: `build_timeout_sec = 600.0`, `network_mode = "public"`, `cpus = 2`, `memory_mb = 4096`. A case-insensitive search of task.toml for `image` returns no match, so neither `[environment].docker_image` nor a `[verifier.environment]` image key exists (that table holds only `network_mode = "public"`). The [environment] block is identical to the frozen template's. task/environment/Dockerfile has active build steps (`FROM node:22-bookworm-slim`, apt-get install of ca-certificates git procps sqlite3, `npm install -g ... express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1`, `COPY instructions/ /instructions/`, `COPY assets/ /assets/`, git init of /app) and is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (diff empty). With no prebuilt image named, these steps are what the harness builds, so the Dockerfile is not dead code. Rule sources agree: workbook row 12, quality-checks.md check 12 ('`[environment].docker_image` is not set while the agent Dockerfile still has active build steps') and staged-task-contract.md ('must be absent while the Dockerfile has active build steps'). Adversarial variants tried: a commented or differently spelled image key, an image key in another table, and a Dockerfile reduced to no build steps; none is present. This is a static configuration property fully decided by the frozen bytes. Evidence index: I recomputed the SHA256 of run_golden.sh and results/runtime.json and both match the index; the scripted golden is stated to have run in the agent image but not through the harness, and the hosted run is on an earlier candidate, so neither is a harness build measurement of these bytes. That gap does not bear on this row.
